story.title: The hidden opportunity
story.headline: Great store systems. Fragmented commercial decisions.
story.explanation: Technology data is useful. But the business question remains unanswered when each function sees only its own system.
story.presenterNotes: Ask the audience which dashboards they already have. Contrast product insight with enterprise decision quality. Avoid calling current tools broken. Industry-specific context: Retail has excellent store systems data, but the buying decisions are distributed across commercial, operations and IT.
story.transition: Next, connect this to start at the board.

lensTalkingPoints.customer: Decision owner and measurable change: Chief commercial officer.
lensTalkingPoints.cisco: Capability test: Cisco networking / wireless — subject to architecture fit.

story.title: Start at the board
story.headline: Lead with growth, cost-to-serve and customer trust.
story.explanation: Begin with strategic demand: decisions and outcomes the leadership team will fund.
story.presenterNotes: Ask for three board objectives and one measurable commitment. Where relevant separate revenue, operating costs, risk and sustainability obligations. Industry-specific context: The executive issue is profitable growth, customer experience, stock availability and estate cost.
story.transition: Next, connect this to follow value across functions.

lensTalkingPoints.customer: Decision owner and measurable change: Chief commercial officer.
lensTalkingPoints.cisco: Capability test: Cisco networking / wireless — subject to architecture fit.

story.title: Follow value across functions
story.headline: A store outcome cuts across operations and functions.
story.explanation: An outcome is shared across functions; costs, owners and evidence are distributed.
story.presenterNotes: Invite stakeholders to identify who controls actions versus who carries cost or benefit. Accessibility, EHS and privacy can change the solution. Industry-specific context: Commercial, merchandising, store operations and facilities each control part of the result.
story.transition: Next, connect this to build the value twin.

lensTalkingPoints.customer: Decision owner and measurable change: Store operations.
lensTalkingPoints.cisco: Capability test: Cisco networking / wireless — subject to architecture fit.

story.title: Build the Value Twin
story.headline: Model store value before building a technical twin.
story.explanation: A Value Twin is a semantic model of customer decisions, signals, assumptions and value — before a full operational digital twin.
story.presenterNotes: Explain the conceptual Value Twin is a linked decision graph: it does NOT need live BMS or a rendered BIM model to begin. Source claims remain provisional. Industry-specific context: The Value Twin connects shopper demand, store operations and facilities without requiring a full digital twin.
story.transition: Next, connect this to reason across signals.

lensTalkingPoints.customer: Decision owner and measurable change: Store operations.
lensTalkingPoints.cisco: Capability test: Cisco security — subject to architecture fit.

story.title: Reason across signals
story.headline: Correlate shopper, energy and fulfilment signals.
story.explanation: Reason over evidence from multiple domains; discover patterns while marking uncertainty and testing causality.
story.presenterNotes: Discuss correlation versus causation. Confirm data access, quality, time alignment, weather, seasonality, shifts, comparable sites and privacy. Industry-specific context: Consider whether peak queues, footfall and staffing are jointly affecting conversion — a testable hypothesis.
story.transition: Next, connect this to test a business hypothesis.

lensTalkingPoints.customer: Decision owner and measurable change: Merchandising.
lensTalkingPoints.cisco: Capability test: Cisco security — subject to architecture fit.

story.title: Test a business hypothesis
story.headline: Test conversion, cost and service hypotheses.
story.explanation: Prioritise measurable interventions, baseline the outcome and design a risk-controlled pilot.
story.presenterNotes: Choose one hypothesis. Agree baseline, test design, owner, benefit formula, risk controls, investment threshold and success/failure triggers. Industry-specific context: An experiment defines interventions and cost-to-serve before the solution architecture.
story.transition: Next, connect this to orchestrate the ecosystem.

lensTalkingPoints.customer: Decision owner and measurable change: Merchandising.
lensTalkingPoints.cisco: Capability test: Cisco security — subject to architecture fit.

story.title: Orchestrate the ecosystem
story.headline: Create repeatable joint partner services per site.
story.explanation: Only now select vendor capabilities, partners, services and commercial models necessary to deliver value.
story.presenterNotes: Do not present the Cisco portfolio as the whole solution. Show OT, integrators, FM/industry experts and partner recurring revenue responsibilities. Industry-specific context: Partners combine store systems, networking, analytics and managed services into repeatable site offers.
story.transition: Next, connect this to prove, learn and expand.

lensTalkingPoints.customer: Decision owner and measurable change: Facilities / Energy.
lensTalkingPoints.cisco: Capability test: Splunk / observability — subject to architecture fit.

story.title: Prove, learn and expand
story.headline: Verify store economics before expanding the estate.
story.explanation: Operate, measure against the counterfactual, report realised value and feed learning into the next opportunity.
story.presenterNotes: Close the loop: evidence-backed impact, governance, operational ownership, changes in assumptions, and scaling into adjacent sites or value streams. Industry-specific context: Use measured pilot uplift and operating costs to decide if the model scales across the estate.
story.transition: Return to a new discovery conversation or choose a different industry pack.
